concept.summary: Nebular theory is the explanation for where our solar system came from. It starts with a cold cloud of gas and dust drifting in space and ends with a star and eight planets. Every step in between is gravity doing one thing: pulling matter toward the densest point, and speeding it up as it goes.
keyIdeas: Gravity pulls inward. Everything else in the story is a consequence of that.
A spinning cloud flattens into a disk for the same reason pizza dough does.

priorKnowledge.label: BEFORE YOU START — YOU ALREADY KNOW THIS
items: Gravity pulls, and pulls harder when things are closer together or more massive (S1.2).
A nebula is a cloud of gas and dust in space (S1.2).

blocks.instruction: These 6 cards are scrambled — they are NOT in the correct order. Read each one, cut it out, and colour or sketch a small illustration for it. Set the six cards aside; you will glue them onto the timeline on the next page once your group agrees on the order.

cards.title: Accretion
cards.text: Clumps of matter farther out in the disk sweep up nearby gas and dust as they orbit, growing larger and larger.

cards.title: A Nebula Drifts
cards.text: A giant cloud of gas and dust — a nebula — exists quietly in space. Nothing is condensing yet.

cards.title: Fusion Ignites
cards.text: The centre finally reaches about 10 million °C. Nuclear fusion begins — a star is born at the centre of the system.

cards.title: A Protostar Forms
cards.text: The densest region of the nebula begins to condense under its own gravity. As it condenses, it heats up.

cards.title: Solar Wind Clears the System
cards.text: Fusion's outward pressure blows the leftover gas and dust out of the system, leaving a star and its planets behind.

cards.title: Spinning and Flattening
cards.text: Gravity pulls material toward the centre. As the cloud collapses inward, it spins faster and flattens into a disk.

blocks.heading: Your Nebular Theory Timeline
blocks.instruction: Glue the whole card — title, description and your drawing — into its matching numbered slot below, in the order the solar system actually forms. Slot 1 happens first. Each slot is sized to match the cards exactly.

prompts: What has to happen before fusion can ignite? Why can't it happen at stage 1?
What would be different about a solar system that formed from a smaller, less massive nebula?

checklist: All six cards are glued down, in order, with nothing loose.
Every card has a drawing on it, not just the words.
Both reflection questions are answered in full sentences.
